identity.name: Sikh state of Banda Singh Bahadur

land.text: the province of Sirhind and its 28 parganas, 'from the Sutlej to the Yamuna', taken from the Mughal governors in 1709-1710

predecessors.note: A rebel state: Banda Singh Bahadur held Sirhind against the Mughals, so the Mughal dossier should carry the matching contest (it has none at writing).

land.text: the pockets Banda still held: the Gurdas Nangal fort, where the Mughals 'broke into the starving garrison' on 7 December 1715

successors.note: The Sikh misls of the 1760s (sikh-confederacy) are a separate later formation, half a century on.

capitals.name: Lohgarh (Mukhlisgarh)
capitals.note: 'He developed Mukhlisgarh and renamed it Lohgarh', where he issued his own mint; lost in December 1710, retaken in March 1712, left in 1713.

capitals.name: Dera Baba Banda Singh (Jammu hills)
capitals.note: 'The Sikhs left Lohgarh and Sadhaura for the Jammu hills and built Dera Baba Banda Singh' (1713); the page does not call it a capital.

rulers.name: Banda Singh Bahadur
rulers.title: Jathedar
rulers.note: Infobox 'Reign (as Jathedar): 26 November 1709 - 7 December 1715'; executed in Delhi on 9 June 1716.

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria draws the whole Sirhind polygon (24,700 km2: 91 cells, Haryana 49, Punjab 29, Himachal Pradesh 10, 75.7-77.5 E, 28.8-31.1 N) from 1709 to 1712. Banda took only Samana in November 1709; Sirhind fell on 12-14 May 1710 and the Mughals' counter-offensive took Lohgarh in December 1710. The page gives no area but describes the province of Sirhind (28 parganas) 'from the Sutlej to the Yamuna', which fits the polygon, so the polygon is kept for 1710 only (new keyframe) and 1709 is Samana.

correction.text: Samana, 'sacked in November 1709' (battle table 28 November 1709), the first land held

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's Sirhind polygon for the year the province was held. 'By the 14th [May 1710] Sikhs entered Sirhind'; Banda held 'the province of Sirhind and its 28 parganas', yielding 3,600,000 rupees a year, from the Shivalik hills to Kunjpura, Karnal and Kaithal; Baj Singh governed Sirhind, Fateh Singh Samana, Ram Singh Thanesar. Saharanpur and Muzaffarnagar in Uttar Pradesh also fell to the Sikhs (outside the polygon; the page gives no date).

correction.text: the province of Sirhind with its 28 parganas, between the Sutlej and the Yamuna

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (bridge, confidence 1): after the Mughal counter-offensive of December 1710 ('on 10 December 1710 he ordered that wherever a Sikh was found, he should be killed') Banda 'left the fort at night for hills and Chamba forests'. The page does not say what Banda held in 1711 or that the Mughals retook Sirhind; only the hill country is kept (the 10 Himachal cells of the polygon).

correction.text: the Shivalik and Chamba hill country to which Banda withdrew

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'In 1712 Banda recaptured Sadhaura and Lohgarh' (Second Battle of Lohgarh, March 1712 in the page's table). Only the Sadhaura-Lohgarh pocket is drawn; the page does not say Sirhind returned.

Cliopatria repeats the Sirhind polygon for 1713-1717. In 1713 'the Sikhs left Lohgarh and Sadhaura for the Jammu hills and built Dera Baba Banda Singh'; Gurdas Nangal was besieged from April to December 1715 and fell on 7 December 1715; Banda was executed on 9 June 1716. The polygon belongs to no year after 1710; the correction is the dera in the Jammu hills, valid 1713-1714, and the Gurdas Nangal fort for 1715 (new keyframe). The shape's tail (1716-1717) is past the end of the state.

correction.text: Dera Baba Banda Singh in the Jammu hills, valid 1713-1714

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'In March 1715, the army under the command of Abd al-Samad Khan drove Banda's forces into Gurdas Nangal'; the Sikhs held out for eight months, until 7 December 1715.

correction.text: the fortified village of Gurdas Nangal, besieged April-December 1715

ledger.note: November 1709: Banda Singh Bahadur takes Samana and founds the first Sikh state. 'In November 1709 he sacked Samana' (battle table 28 November 1709); infobox 'Reign (as Jathedar): 26 November 1709'. Guru Gobind Singh had given him the title Bahadur in September 1708 and died on 7 October 1708.
Early 1710: Sadhaura falls to the Sikhs. The text gives no date; the battle table lists the Battle of Sadaura in early 1710.

12-14 May 1710: the Sikhs win at Chappar Chiri and enter Sirhind. 'Both sides faced off in Chappar Chiri on 12 May 1710'; 'By the 14th Sikhs entered Sirhind.' Banda then abolished the zamindari system and held the province, 'extended from the Sutlej to the Yamuna', with a revenue of 3,600,000 rupees.

region.text: the province of Sirhind and its 28 parganas

ledger.note: December 1710: the first Battle of Lohgarh. The Mughals under Bahadur Shah besiege Lohgarh with '60,000 troops' (the page gives no siege date) and Banda escapes by night to the hills; on 10 December 1710 the emperor ordered every Sikh killed.

1711: Sirhind is out of Sikh hands. The page does not say the Mughals retook Sirhind or when; the loss is inferred from the retreat to the hills and the Mughal order of 10 December 1710 (confidence 1).

region.text: the rest of the province of Sirhind

ledger.note: March 1712: Banda retakes Sadhaura and Lohgarh (Second Battle of Lohgarh, March 1712 in the page's table; 'In 1712, Banda recaptured Sadhaura and Lohgarh').

1713: the Sikhs leave Lohgarh and Sadhaura. 'The Sikhs left Lohgarh and Sadhaura for the Jammu hills and built Dera Baba Banda Singh.' The page does not say who took the pocket; the Mughals are my reading.

region.text: Lohgarh and Sadhaura, left for the Jammu hills

ledger.note: 1713: Banda builds his dera in the Jammu hills. The page names no local ruler or state.

region.text: Dera Baba Banda Singh in the Jammu hills

ledger.note: March 1715: Abd al-Samad Khan's army drives Banda's forces into Gurdas Nangal; the siege runs April-December ('eight months').
7 December 1715: 'the Mughals broke into the starving garrison' and captured Banda and his companions.
December 1715: the first Sikh state ends with Banda's capture; he was blinded and beheaded in Delhi on 9 June 1716. The infobox gives no 'disestablished' date.

region.text: Gurdas Nangal, the last Sikh pocket

wars.name: Banda Singh Bahadur's Sirhind campaign
wars.outcome: Samana sacked in November 1709, Sadhaura in early 1710, Sirhind taken on 12-14 May 1710 after Chappar Chiri.

wars.name: Mughal counter-offensive and the sieges of Lohgarh and Gurdas Nangal
wars.outcome: Lohgarh fell in December 1710 (first battle); Banda retook Sadhaura and Lohgarh in 1712 (second battle, March 1712), left for the Jammu hills in 1713, was besieged at Gurdas Nangal from April 1715 and captured on 7 December 1715; executed in Delhi on 9 June 1716.
wars.note: The 'Battle of Lohgarh' page is a disambiguation page (First Battle 1710, Second Battle 1712-1713); the two articles were not opened (page budget).

certainty.note: The page gives a province of 28 parganas 'from the Sutlej to the Yamuna' and named forts, not boundaries; the pockets after 1710 are forts with a radius.

notes:
Two pages opened (budget 1-2): Banda Singh Bahadur, and the 'Battle of Lohgarh' disambiguation page, which was empty of detail; the First and Second Battle of Lohgarh articles were not opened (budget). No page gives a month for the December 1710 loss of Lohgarh or says what happened to the province of Sirhind afterwards: the 1711 loss of Sirhind and the 1711 and 1713-1715 pockets are bridges at confidence 1-2.

Typed rebel (rule 5): a rebel state that held land for six years. Cliopatria's 'Sikhs' row (1709-1717) is the first Sikh state of Banda Singh Bahadur, not the Sikh people or the later Sikh Confederacy (1762) and Sikh Empire (1799); the Wikipedia title in the Cliopatria row is 'Sikhs' (the people), the state article is 'Banda Singh Bahadur' (infobox allegiance 'Khalsa; First Sikh State').

Cliopatria error: the same 24,700 km2 Sirhind polygon is drawn for 1709-1717; it holds only from May to December 1710.

The Mughal dossier (mughal-empire) has no contest or loss event for Banda's rising at writing; a gap-filler should add contest_start 1709/1710 and contest_end 1715 for Sirhind against 'sikhs', and the Mughal recovery of Sirhind (undated on this page).

Not settled: Saharanpur and Muzaffarnagar (taken by the Sikhs, undated, outside the Cliopatria polygon); the Jalandhar Doab and any sack of Lahore (page silent); the gazetteer lacks Samana, Sadhaura, Lohgarh, Sirhind, Gurdas Nangal and the Dera (coordinates used).
